description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Expand and strengthen coverage of both facility and community interventions; Improve diagnostics including the optimizing new tools to match the increased number of people to be tested;Reach underserved communities in hard to reach areas; and Strategically increase public-private mix coverage.This activity will increase the number of TB patients detected, treated, and notified of their status in 14 states (Bauchi, Kaduna, Katsina, Kano, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Anambra, Akwa Ibom, Benue, Cross River, Delta, Imo, and Rivers). It will also strengthen public private partnerships and alliances with health and related professional organizations, including faith-based associations, to influence their constituencies and communities to implement TB control interventions. This activity will serve as a platform to expand TB care, treatment, and notification services to all public and private health facilities in target states and will facilitate the accomplishment of statewide TB screening and treatment targets. It will also leverage TB platforms to support equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines for all eligible persons in seven selected states. The activity will partner with federal and state ministries of health and other relevant government agencies, as well as the formal and informal private health sector to screen 9,185,965 persons for TB and diagnose and treat 54,978 TB patients. The activity will continue to build the capacity of the national and state TB programs to conduct real-time surveillance for TB patients and establish links to quality care and treatment programs.This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2 and is closely aligned with Goal 1 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan...
